evidence:
Scope: all three scored dimensions are mode="batched", aggregation="weighted_mean" (scored/functional/judge.toml:3,21; polish/judge.toml:3,15; visual/judge.toml:3,15). Gates render/constraints are mode=batched with aggregation="all_pass" (gates/*/judge.toml:15) and are exempt per workbook row 38 and deterministic row 5. scoring.toml: gates 0.0, functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, functional floor 0.05.

Independence wording present in every scored prompt:
- functional/prompt.md:13 "Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own if that is possible without the broken feature..." plus :7 "give that criterion its lowest score ... state what you observed, and move on", :23 "Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row", :53 per-outcome NOT EXERCISED with "Preserve every completed independent observation."
- polish/prompt.md:12 "Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures." plus :7 ("move on") and :18 (preserve completed observations).
- visual/prompt.md:12 "Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures." plus :7, :14 ("Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row") and :16.

No stop-on-first-failure wording: grep of all scored prompts, judge.toml criteria and app_context.md for stop/abort/halt/first fail/do not continue/zero-all patterns found only the global browser-gate zeroing (functional:13, polish:12, visual:12), which is the required hard gate (check 29), not a cascade from one criterion to the rest. The only conditional zeroes inside criteria are self-scoped (polish judge.toml hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread: 'this row is 0'; functional:51 'hro_restart is 0' if restart_app fails).

Cross-criterion references in functional/judge.toml are de-duplication scope notes, not dependencies: :65 'Arrival of several cards together belongs to hro_bulk_move'; :110 'Overfill by a multi-card move belongs to hro_bulk_places and by undo to hro_undo_full'; :371 'Clearing the box after sending is graded in hro_msg_compose'; :380 'graded only in hro_candidate_private ... graded in hro_msg_exchange'. These prevent one miss from zeroing several rows, which supports this check.

Adversarial reasoning: (a) Weak app that could wrongly pass: wording does not create a pass path; independence only preserves observed successes, and each refusal row requires its own positive control (functional:13). (b) Conforming alternative that could wrongly fail via cascade: an app where, e.g., multi-card move is broken would lose hro_bulk_move but the prompt tells the judge to re-run setup on a new job and keep other rows; a shared-setup failure is explicitly not a conjunctive bundle. Only failure of the global backend gate zeroes everything, which is the intended gate. No cascade wording found.

Integrity: sha256 of frozen functional/polish/visual prompt.md (0cbb5e3d..., 34653321..., 704971dd...) and functional/judge.toml (0a864ac1...) each appear in manifest.json; the three frozen prompts are byte-identical to the live projects/ copies. Task wording is consistent with (and stronger than) the template's 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure'.

Limits (not required for this wording row, recorded honestly): check-batched-independence-wording.py was applied manually, not executed; raw-evidence-index.json states no configured judge run exists, so actual judge adherence to independent scoring (e.g. under budget exhaustion in the very long 45-criterion functional batch) is unmeasured. That runtime question belongs to workload/full-grading rows; it does not change this row's prompt-wording verdict.
